osaka_spys_oasis_namba.gf_detail: The shop describes itself as serving gluten-free food and drinks, and explains on its site that it does not use gluten (「グルテンは使わないんです」). Tabelog's introduction says "completely gluten-free dishes and drinks", and a September 2026 reviewer reports "all products are 100% gluten-free", with no dairy or white sugar. Gluten-free drinks are served even at the bar, for example a GF Red Eye. Tabelog notes allergy information is available. The shop's stated reason is health rather than celiac safety, and no cross-contact controls are described, so confirm if you are celiac.
osaka_spys_oasis_namba.vegan_detail: A separate vegan-and-gluten-free curry line on the official menu: root-vegetable curry, soy-mince and red-pepper salsa curry, and a pumpkin, banana, mango, corn and chickpea curry (¥1,700 each, ¥1,800 for two, ¥1,900 for three), with vegan toppings. The house three-curry set contains chicken, pork and mackerel, and the soup is made with chicken.
osaka_spys_oasis_namba.hours_raw: Mon–Wed, Fri–Sat: lunch 11:30–15:00, bar 18:00–24:00 (one-drink minimum); Sun and holidays 11:30–15:00 and 17:00–22:00; closed Thursdays; changes on social media (official site). Online booking only, no phone reservations (official site).
osaka_spys_oasis_namba.notes: [Curry · gluten-free yakuzen spice curry by Dotonbori] A 14-seat curry café and evening bar run on a "food as medicine" concept by a yakuzen (medicinal-cooking) specialist. Everything is gluten-free by the shop's own account. The signature is three curries to mix: a soy-milk, onion, tomato and ginger chicken-breast curry; a black-sesame and red-miso pork-and-hijiki keema; and a mackerel and lotus-root "green Popeye" curry. Each is tangy and spiced, and they come together into one flavour when mixed. They sit over basmati and 15-grain rice (Simple ¥1,600; Standard ¥2,000 with soup, salad and toppings). A separate vegan line covers root-vegetable, soy-mince salsa and tropical chickpea curries. At night it becomes a bar with GF drinks, natural wine and tapas. English menu; book online.

chef_bio.background: Official site: yakuzen spice curry made by a yakuzen meister (薬膳マイスター), on the principle 医食同源 ("food and medicine share one source").
chef_bio.philosophy: 「医食同源のコンセプトの元、栄養価はもちろん、身体に優しい食材を厳選」 (official site).

osaka_old_cairo_cafe.notes: [Middle Eastern · an Egyptian café and shisha bar in Amemura] A moody, Egyptian-styled café on the 3rd floor of a building in Amerikamura that serves lunch and runs as a shisha bar at night, with occasional dance shows. Staff explain the dishes and share stories about Egypt. Order koshari, the national dish of rice, macaroni and lentils in tomato sauce under crisp fried onions, with garlic vinegar and chili oil to season. There's also ta'ameya (Egyptian falafel), hummus with pita, a rich, garlicky molokhia soup, and shish tawook chicken plates (about ¥1,600–1,800). Finish with baklava or kahk and hibiscus juice or mint tea. Tabelog lists vegan, vegetarian and halal options. Opening days vary, so check Instagram or book. On event nights, food can take an hour.

osaka_creperie_alcyon_namba.notes: [Sweets · Namba's famous crêpes and galettes] A 50-seat French crêperie up steep stairs just south of Dotonbori, named to Tabelog's Sweets WEST "100" in 2023 and 2026, with a takeout line downstairs. The crêpes, made with French flour, Échiré butter and salt, are crisp at the edge and chewy inside. The plain Échiré butter and sugar is the one regulars call the best they've had. At lunch, try a daily galette from the blackboard, say beef stew over mashed potato and cheese, or tandoori chicken, in the crêperie lunch (¥2,200, October 2026). There's also a milk-jam crêpe set with vanilla gelato (¥1,480), quiche and Mont Blanc. The takeout queue is about 10 minutes. Cash only.

Finish with kamameshi, rice cooked to order in an iron pot, like the chicken soboro and burdock, so order it early. Ordering is by LINE. The upstairs can get smoky from the grill, and there's a pleasant terrace. Note the name: Tabelog lists it as Nakamoto, while several 2026 reviews call it "Yakitori to Kamameshi Gotchin".

osaka_ichiban_malatang_nipponbashi.notes: [Chinese · malatang with a beef-bone white broth in Nippombashi] A clean, 20-seat malatang shop a few minutes from Nippombashi, relaxed enough when reviewers came that you can take your time at the ingredient case. The difference is the broth: beef bone, and the original white version is rich enough at zero spice to taste like ramen soup. Vegetables soaked in it, broccoli especially, are the reviewers' pick. Spice runs from 0 up to a numbing level 3 at least, and chili oil comes on the side. One mala fan ranks it third of 19 places tried. Spend over ¥1,000, as most do, and a can from the fridge is free. The aroma inside takes a minute to get used to.

osaka_roman_amemura.notes: [Ramen · late-night abura-soba in Amemura] A new Roman shop, opened on 20 September 2026 among the Amerika-mura live houses and open until 5 am. Roman is an Osaka brand that began in Morinomiya in 2022. The abura-soba (¥850) is the plain, steady kind, on thick, curly house-made noodles cut short enough to slurp. Reviewers douse it in vinegar and chili oil, add garlic or kimchi, and find it not greasy at all. The mazesoba (¥1,000) comes with more sauce than expected and a strong soy edge, and there is a Taiwanese mazesoba. After 10 pm the shop adds something the name doesn't promise: a smooth, milky tonkotsu ramen on thin straight noodles (¥900; ¥1,100 piled with chashu), creamy but light enough for that hour. You buy a ticket at the machine; about three tables and eight counter seats.

chef_bio.background: The Roman brand started in Morinomiya, Osaka, in 2022 (October 2026 review); new Kobe Motomachi and Kishiwada shops opened the month before this one (September 2026 review).

osaka_juroku_namba_bettei.notes: [Korean · Japanese-Korean sundubu in Namba Walk] A calm, 17-seat sundubu shop in the Namba Walk underground mall, by Nippombashi Station, here for about a year by autumn 2026. The soft-tofu stew is rich and sweet beneath the heat. Spice runs from 1 to 4, with 2 as standard. Several reviewers found 3 easy going, and 1 not spicy at all. Sets come with rice and three small sides, and a scoop of lychee sorbet arrives at the end. The Namba-only sundubu ramen puts noodles in the stew (one visitor added rice for ¥100), though one reviewer compared the noodles to boiled dried noodles rather than real ramen. Other picks are the grilled-pork sundubu with clams and minced meat, grilled-cheese sundubu ramen, and Wakan herb cold noodles. The manager runs the floor attentively; you buy a ticket at the entrance. Tabelog spells the name "Juraku"; the kana じゅろく reads Juroku.

chef_bio.background: Japanese-Korean (wakan) sundubu specialist; "なんば別邸" branch name (Tabelog). A reviewer has seen it on TV recently (October 2026).

osaka_kibunya_dotonbori.notes: [Ramen · Wakayama-style ramen until dawn on Dotonbori] A Wakayama-style ramen shop by the Sōemonchō end of Dotonbori, open from 9 am until 5 am (6 am on Fridays, Saturdays and the night before a holiday), full of tourists from home and abroad. The Kishu Wakayama ramen (¥950 before tax, September 2026) is a soy-tonkotsu bowl on thin noodles. There's a light option, a rich one, and an "aged" ramen, which one July 2026 reviewer found just right in flavor and fat as an after-drinks bowl. Also on the menu: a shrimp-heavy tsukemen, and in September a limited Japanese-style tororo cold ramen (¥1,210) with chicken chashu and a tempura egg on chilled thin noodles. Opinions split in autumn 2026. One returning visitor found the broth weak and lukewarm, while another drank every drop. Watch the menu: the big number is before tax. You pay on the way out.

osaka_susuruka_susuranka_shinsaibashi.notes: [Ramen · mapo tofu ramen under Higashi-Shinsaibashi] The Shinsaibashi branch of a mapo-tofu-ramen specialist from Naramachi, Nara, in a calm, chic basement with a long counter, tables and a projector. It is open until 4 am Friday to Sunday. The signature is mapo tofu ladled hot over the noodles. The Nara shop describes made-to-order mapo on smooth, chewy medium-thick noodles, and one reviewer ended up sweating and ordering rice for the leftover sauce. A limited bowl changes through the year. October 2026 brought a seafood and meat-miso mazesoba (¥1,300) with egg yolk, fish powder, chives and bean sprouts on thick, chewy noodles. Summer had a chilled basil mapo ramen. Finish with saba-dashi rice (¥300). The shop says it offers vegetarian and halal options; ask the staff. One October 2026 visitor found it empty at Friday lunch and had to call for service.

osaka_casablanca_namba_riverside.notes: [Café · Mediterranean breakfast-to-midnight on the Dotonbori River] A bright café-restaurant on the ground floor of S-Front Dotonbori, opened July 2025. A riverside terrace (dogs welcome) is the landmark, and it runs from a 7 am breakfast to a late bar. The menu is Middle Eastern and Mediterranean, and the shop says it covers vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free diners; tell them when you book. The reviewed vegan plate is the domestic-corn tartine on rye bread, with sweet charred corn, hummus, avocado, tomato and marinated onions. One September 2026 diner found that nothing felt missing. Falafel pita sandwiches and grilled-chicken shawarma lead at lunch. Breakfast runs to English breakfast, Turkish eggs and a smoked-salmon bagel. The coffee is roasted in-house. English menu and English-speaking staff.

chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog): a barista roasts small batches of beans in-house, including Ethiopian and Colombian; private parties for up to 60.

osaka_menya_masamune_edion_namba.notes: [Ramen · Sendai abura-soba on the EDION 9F ramen floor] An abura-soba shop from Sendai that opened on the Namba Ramen Ichiza floor in December 2025. The original Sendai abura-soba (¥1,150) is mild on its own: chewy medium-thick noodles in a light sauce, under grilled "toro" meat soft enough to melt, half an egg, green onion and nori. You build it yourself with the vinegar and chili oil the sign tells you to add (twice), plus pepper or Sichuan pepper. Beyond it are a punchy G-style bowl with pork fat and garlic, a Taiwanese mazesoba (¥1,150), a rich two-cheese mazesoba with egg yolk (¥1,200) and a tsukimi abura-soba with tororo (¥950). Summer brought a chilled soy-milk tantan mazesoba. There's also a clear Date's salt ramen. Mix the leftover sauce with rice (¥100), or add beef-tongue curry (¥400). Spacious, clean, counter and tables.

osaka_tsukemen_suzume_amemura.notes: [Ramen · Amemura's original niboshi tsukemen] Suzume's 12-seat counter in Amerika-mura has been pouring tsukemen since 2010, and people still queue outside. The dipping broth is niboshi-based but smooth and deep. One reviewer, back after 15 years in Tokyo, still calls it the original taste of tsukemen. It's rich with seafood umami, for thick, chewy noodles you can have at 200 g or 300 g for the same price. The cult order is the spicy tsukemen (¥1,000), with heat levels; level 2 is rich rather than fierce. Swap in the red, chili-infused noodles for ¥30. The special (¥1,300) adds thick, tender chashu. Mix, taste, then add vinegar and chili oil. Some long-time regulars feel it isn't quite what it was. Cash only.

osaka_kanyu_micchan.notes: [Korean · yukgaejang noodles behind Hotel Royal Classic] A 10-seat Korean lunch counter in Ura-Namba, on the street behind Hotel Royal Classic Osaka, open since 2020 and often with a line. Everyone orders the yukgaejang noodles (¥1,200, October 2026): a spicy-sweet beef soup packed with chunky meat and vegetables on thin noodles, hot enough to make you sweat. Add a soft-boiled egg to cool your tongue. The set adds a grilled rare harami rice bowl that some think beats the noodles. The small size is bigger than it looks, and you can tip the leftover rice into the soup. Korean cold noodles suit the spice-shy. Cash only, and smoking is allowed.

osaka_wagyu_ramen_nipponbashi.notes: [Ramen · course-style wagyu ramen in Nippombashi] A new evening ramen counter that opened on 29 June 2026 in the former Men no Hiromiya space by Nippombashi. It is a new concept from the Dotonbori tonkatsu shop "Ganso 5cm Katsu Don" (review), and the price matches the show: ¥3,900 for 100 g of wagyu, up to ¥10,900 for 450 g. It runs like a little course. A flying-fish dashi with gold leaf comes first. Then a grilled flying fish is cut with scissors and ground into powder in a mortar, and the chef adds it to your bowl. The ramen is a low-viscosity chicken-bone and flying-fish shoyu, light and smooth with a mild seafood sweetness, on chewy medium-thin wavy noodles from Taiyo Seimenjo. The seasoned wagyu flank arrives on a small teppan over a burner so you can cook it to your liking. Only one review so far (July 2026).

osaka_chuka_shunsai_morimoto.notes: [Chinese · Tabelog 100 yodare chicken and mapo in a Shinsaibashi basement] A 48-seat basement Chinese restaurant off Shinsaibashi-suji, on Tabelog's Chinese 100 list in 2021, 2023 and 2024, and the lunch line proves it. The dish everyone orders is yodare chicken, buried under cilantro in a sesame-thick, spicy sauce you toss like a salad; ask for green onion if you don't like cilantro. The mapo tofu arrives bubbling in a clay pot, authentic and properly spicy. The dan dan noodles are rich. Lunch sets come with egg-drop soup, side dishes good enough to be mains, almond jelly and free rice refills. Go after 2 pm to skip the queue. Dinner adds xiao long bao, spicy chicken and water spinach (draft beer is ¥950), and booking is wise.

osaka_horie_hakkodo.notes: [Set meals · fermented-food lunch on Orange Street] A roomy set-meal café among the clothing shops of Horie's Orange Street, built around fermented food. The shop says it uses pesticide-free, additive-free ingredients and handmade or traditionally made seasonings. Most people order the fermented kara-age set, crisp outside and remarkably moist inside, with five small sides. For a meat-free lunch there's the healthy fermented vegetable set, with fragrant miso soup and fermented-enzyme brown rice that turns sweet as you chew (July 2026); ask whether the miso soup uses fish stock. There's also a fried mackerel set, plus fermented shakes and seasonal enzyme juices. Order on the touch panel. It gets busy at lunch, so come early or book.

osaka_cafe_morning_box.notes: [Café · hotel-lobby coffee with vegan bakes by Nagahoribashi] The ground-floor café of HOTEL MORNING BOX, a minute from Nagahoribashi and calm even at weekends. It has two floors of tables and sofas, plus counters with outlets where people work and take calls. The shop lists organic and vegan deli options at lunch, and reviewers mention a range of vegan baked goods. The bakes are additive-free and change daily. The cinnamon carrot cake is the Instagram favourite, and the canelé is made with rice flour. Weekends bring a rice-flour French toast; the summer 2026 version had a whole peach and Earl Grey, with mascarpone, so it isn't vegan. Breakfast includes an eggs Benedict (¥1,800) that one guest found more ham-and-eggs. Coffee is the specialty, served from 8 am to 10:30 pm.

Every bowl lists calories and macros. You choose from six base concepts, one of them "Healthy & high-protein for vegans" (shop text), then customize the toppings and dressing. The house PROTEIN LAB bowl (¥1,600) comes with very tender chicken breast, and there's a Mexican bowl (¥1,480). An acai bowl (¥1,600) comes half-frozen with banana, berries, kiwi, coconut and granola; honey is only added if you say yes. Order and pay at the register, then sit anywhere.

Both come on house-made noodles blended with German rye, nutty and almost soba-like, with grape pepper on the rim to stir in. The tsukemen takes a different direction: rye flat noodles in a creamy duck dip with a Kishu-mikan or cherry sauce and a Madeira accent. The Namba-only duck skewers come with three condiments, and there's a house GION DUCK BEER. The menu uses emoji, and staff explain it. Cashless.

osaka_kinryu_ramen_sennichimae.notes: [Ramen · Osaka's 24-hour dragon-sign classic] One of the long-running Kinryu Ramen shops of Namba, under the giant dragon sign and open around the clock. The menu is just Kinryu ramen (¥900, October 2026) or chashu ramen. Buy a ticket by the door, hand it in, and collect your bowl when called. The broth is a white pork-and-chicken soup with soy, lighter than it looks and smooth rather than greasy, with two kinds of chashu even in the regular bowl. The fun is at the counter: free, unlimited kimchi, spicy garlic chives, garlic and rice, which turn the mild soup into a stamina bowl. You sit on low tatami platforms without backrests, and you might wonder about shoes. It's built for after drinking, or a ten-minute breakfast.

The draw is the free, unlimited chopped green onion; some pile the bowl high. The broth is a mild tonkotsu with medium-thin noodles, firmness to order, and quick service. Another found the taste and service simply average.

osaka_mercy_vegan_ramen_bakuromachi.notes: [Ramen · vegan, gluten-free ramen in Bakuromachi] A spacious, clean ramen shop that opened on 29 January 2026, a new concept from MERCY Vegan Factory. Everything is plant-based and free of the five pungent vegetables, and the ramen is gluten-free. The noodles are medium-thick curly rice-flour noodles from Hokkaido, chewy and bouncy. The shio ramen (¥1,870) is a light, low-viscosity kombu broth with a touch of lemon. The yakuzen soy-milk dan dan noodles (¥2,420; ¥2,200 in July) come loaded with vegetables and warming herbs but only mildly spicy. Summer 2026 added a sesame-vinegar cold noodle (¥2,200). Prices are high for ramen, and one visitor switched to lemonade and salt bread. Outside the ramen, a sister shop's release warns that some items may contain wheat, so ask.

osaka_paprika_shokudo_vegan.notes: [Vegan · all-vegan organic set meals near Yotsubashi] A long-running all-vegan organic restaurant, open since 2014, two minutes from Yotsubashi Station. It's natural and stylish inside, with a shaded terrace deck and a retail shelf by the door. The most popular order is the soy-meat kara-age set: fried in premium canola oil with a house Japanese-style sauce, organic soy-milk mayonnaise and organic sesame. It comes with an organic salad, low-sodium miso soup and pesticide-free brown rice. The soy-meat hamburg with vegan cheese is hearty enough to win over meat-eaters. The menu is wide, and a vegetarian visitor from Australia came back after ten years. Order by QR code at the table. It's popular, so book, especially for lunch. Gluten isn't addressed anywhere, so ask.

osaka_maren_shinsaibashi.notes: [Ramen · chicken-paitan mazesoba until 6 am in Shinsaibashi] A branch of MAREN, a mazesoba shop with its main store in Kitashinchi, open since June 2026 from 11 am to 6 am. It's roomier and nicer than a typical ramen counter, and most customers are visitors from abroad. The skewers are big: plump shrimp, excellent pork, a soft quail egg (best with the white soy sauce), plus tulip wings and asparagus. Dip in the special sauce, grilled salt or white soy, and start with doteyaki. Frying happens downstairs, so the second floor stays free of oil smells. On busy nights the kitchen can lag, with a 30-minute wait for skewers in October 2026.

The owner runs it alone, serving ramen at lunch and Chinese dishes with ramen in the evening. It's usually quiet. The house favourite is the shoyu (¥900; special ¥1,350), balanced between sharpness and richness on a carefully made dashi. The shio is a golden broth clear enough to see the bottom of the bowl, topped with pork rare chashu, chicken chashu, shiso and menma. Closed Tuesdays.

The reliable orders are koh muu yang, grilled pork neck charred outside with a spicy sauce, and gai yang chicken thigh with a nam pla dip. For a late finish there's pho in a hot pot, with mango pudding or coconut ice cream. Portions suit two or three people sharing. A long-time regular thinks prices have crept up.

Summer brings a chilled abura-soba (¥890), and the half fried rice is ¥490. A lunch mix of tourists and local office workers.

osaka_menya_taniguchi_namba.notes: [Ramen · lunchtime chicken paitan and shellfish broth west of Namba] A lunch-only ramen counter of about eight seats a short walk west of Namba Station; one reviewer recalls it as an izakaya by night. osaka_ippudo_horie.notes: [Ramen · Ippudo in Minami-Horie, with a branch-only shoyu tonkotsu] Hakata Ippudo's Horie branch, three minutes from Yotsubashi. osaka_gadouya_iekei_minatomachi.notes: [Ramen · Oudouya-line iekei by JR Namba, open from 7 am] A Yokohama iekei shop in the basement of Minatomachi River Place, a minute from JR Namba, in the direct line of the famous Oudouya. Open December 2024, it runs from 7 am to 3 am and still has a 15-person queue after midnight. The ramen (¥1,000) is a pork-bone soy broth with the sharp soy edge of the style and pork-and-chicken umami, on chewy medium-thick noodles, with two big slices of chashu, spinach and three nori sheets. The smoked chashu is the star of the chashu ramen and chashu rice. Order firmness, richness and oil to taste, then load up on the table garlic, chopped ginger and mayonnaise. The fried horumon is a known side. One devotee calls it Osaka's No. 1 iekei; the saltiness varies visit to visit. Cash only.

osaka_kitan_in_hozenji.notes: [Yakiniku · a 10-seat aged-wagyu omakase in Hozenji Yokocho] A reservation-only counter of ten seats in Hozenji Yokocho, on Tabelog's yakiniku and grill 100 lists every year from 2023 to 2026. There's one seating at 7 pm and one menu, the ¥19,800 omakase, and bookings run months out. It plays like meat kaiseki more than a grill: a broth of wagyu bones and water with a touch of clam, a yukhoe, aged tuna and seasonal plates, all built on aged Matsusaka and aged Miyazaki wagyu bought straight from producers. At the end you can have as much yakiniku as you like, though one diner was already full by then; the chefs grill it in front of you. Wine pairings are good. A 10% service charge applies. A September 2026 review says a restaurant group runs it.
